newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels airport aims for 100mins cargo turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Brussels airport aims for 100mins cargo turnaround.

text.p: Belgium's air cargo community is working on a project to turn Brussels airport into a "100 minutes cargo airport", the vice-chairman of the Belgian air cargo managers' association(ACMAB), Marcel Buelens said
This is a concept to facilitate freight being delivered within 100 minutes or picked-up within 100 minutes, he said.
The Belgian airport authority, airlines, forwarders, customs and handlers, all meet each six weeks to work on the 100 minute concept.
"There has been very positive feedback from the working group. Problems that took months or even years to sort out before can now be solved more quickly."
"Because everyone is there, around the table we can all work together to cut the time down and make the airport more efficient," he said.
For instance, said Buelens, there is a rule that cargo has to be ready by the aircraft 90 minutes before departure but it is often not loaded until 15 minutes before the aircraft takes- off.
"We can easily save half an hour on this process, shaving more time off the process and streamlining the cargo flow."
Transit from the truck to the aircraft or vice versa will hopefully be 100 minutes eventually, he added.
"It is quite a challenge but through the group we are finding ways of saving time."
But he admits it will probably be another 18 months to two years before Brussels is truly a 100 minute airport. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
